questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere with nice weather, food and a different culture. It was also important to me that the city had good transportation opportunities so I could visit other cities during my stay.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, I was provided with most of it

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't remember receiving any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found it through
spotahome.com
. It was located well but it was a bit expensive compared to what other students were able to find.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find something close to the metro and in walking/biking distance from the city centre. Be aware that the metro stops running a bit past midnight both during the week and weekends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wish there had been better options to live on campus

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration proces was easy. The first two weeks, it is possible to switch between classes, and it was very easy to change classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I had looked at from home were taking place at the same time, so it was a bit difficult to make a schedule that worked, since I had to have 5 courses to fit. But I still ended up getting most of the ones I wanted. Some of the courses I had looked at were at a different campus, so I didn't end up taking those.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be stressed about it and ask for help from the mobility office or other exchange students if any problems occur.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were 6 ECTS point so the level felt easier than at home. There was not really homework or that much material that had to be read before hand. The level of the exams was also a bit lower than what im used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, I did not have any books during my exchange, everything is taught in class (with some material online). No group work. There is not lectures and seminars like at home, but only lectures with smaller classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International, European, and Comparative Environmental Law
Access to Justice in a Multilevel Constitutional System and Human Rights
Comparative Constitutional Traditions
Law and Policies of Social Rights Protection in Europe
Comparative Labour Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend Comparative Constitutional Traditions! the professor is very good and the subjects were super interesting and relevant to understand what is going on in the world today

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Metro card was less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were not any social activities arranged by Unimi. But there were many activities hosted by Erasmus other places in the city.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to some of the Erasmus activities especially in the beginning when everyone is new.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are local markets every Tuesday and Saturday around the city. I also recommend taking the train from Milano Central to visit cities nearby like Firenze, Como, Bologna, Parma, Napoli, Rome, etc. I can also recommend going for a day-trip to Lugano to hike.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not socialize a lot with local students myself, but just be open and approach them, they were all super friendly once you start talking.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything is going in a bit slower tempo, which was difficult at first but very enjoyable to try.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open and enjoy it while it lasts

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When choosing courses, look at the location for the campus. Some are taking place outside of the city. If you have time, attend an italian course before going.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience another culture and make new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I didn't know any Italian beforehand.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
